title: A repeated security incident escalates penalties even when the earlier incident belonged to a different Prime
content:
A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.2.3.2 provides that where a new incident "reflects the same or a substantially similar circumstance as a previous Incident in the Registry, the new Incident shall be subject to an escalation multiplier applied to its financial penalty, as determined by the Core Council. **This applies regardless of whether the earlier Incident involved the same Prime.**"

That last sentence converts the Registry from a disciplinary record into a mandatory curriculum. It is paired with A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.2.3.1, which expects Prime Agents "to review the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry on an ongoing basis and to independently incorporate mitigations and controls based on relevant prior incidents into their Spell-development related processes."

The usual justification for escalating repeat penalties is that the offender has demonstrated they did not learn. Here the theory is different: the *ecosystem* has learned, publicly, and failing to absorb a published lesson is the culpable act. Ignorance of another Prime's incident is no defence.

This is how the framework makes a security failure produce ecosystem-wide benefit rather than only a local fix. The trade-off is that it penalizes an actor for something they did not do and may not have seen — defensible only as long as the Registry stays small, well-described and genuinely readable. A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.5.0.6.1 currently lists no incidents at all, so the obligation is cheap today and grows monotonically with the corpus.
description: Every Prime must monitor the shared Registry and import mitigations from others' failures; the escalation multiplier prices in the fact that the lesson was already publicly available.
